newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X says seven suits filed against it.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X says seven suits filed against it.

text.p: Bre-X Minerals Ltd said on Wednesday it learned of seven complaints filed in the United States, which named Bre-X and some of its current and past officers and directors.

The suits, which were previously reported, were filed in federal courts in New York, Texas, California, Georgia, and Washington, and they made claims under U.S. securities laws as well as certain state laws, the company said in a statement.
Bre-X gave details of the complaints, but did not comment further on the court actions.

The complaints were brought on behalf of individuals as well as purported classes of purchasers of Bre-X common shares and, in one case, purchasers of the shares of Bre-X affiliate Bresea Resources Ltd.

"In substance, all the complaints allege that Bre-X statements to the public about the size and nature of the gold deposits at the Busang project have been materially false, as have Bre-X statements to the public about the extent and nature of the Bre-X ownership interest in the property and Bre-X's right to participate in it," the Calgary-based gold prospector said in a statement.

Bre-X has been in the eye of the storm since preliminary tests by its partner Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc on the Busang gold property in Indonesia indicated the deposit may contain "insignificant" amounts of gold.
The announcement prompted panic selling of Bre-X shares last month, lopping almost C$3 billion, or more than 80 percent, from the company's stock market value.

Bre-X has said an independent audit of the Busang project would confirm Bre-X's estimate of 71 million ounces of gold, potentially the richest in the world. Results of the audit will be released in late April over early May.
Bre-X officials named in the complaints included Chief Executive David Walsh and John Felderhof, Bre-X's head of exploration.
Bre-X said the complaints also alleged that the statements were made with the intention of deceiving members of the investing public and with the intention that the price of Bre-X shares would rise.

The company said the complaints alleged that made it possible for company insiders to profit from the rise in the share price by selling shares at a time when they knew the truth about the mineral deposits and the Bre-X interest at Busang but members of the investing public did not.

Some trades by Walsh and others in 1996 were controversial because they occurred shortly after Bre-X learned that its preliminary license had been canceled by Indonesia, something the company did not make public until last October.

Walsh has said he considered the revoked license "non-material" information because Bre-X's claim to Busang was in good standing. "At no time was the ground not legally held and the revocation was a non-material fact," he said in a recent interview.
The Ontario Securities Commission, Canada's top securities regulator, is probing Bre-X for possible violations of insider trading and disclosure laws.
The details of the allegations in the complaints vary somewhat from case to case.

* New Madras Limited Partnership v. Bre-X Minerals, Ltd., David G. Walsh, and John B. Felderhof. 97 CV. 0901, United States District Court, Northern District of Georgia, Atlanta Division. This is a purported class action in which plaintiff alleges violations of Section 10(b) and 20(a) of the Securities Exchange Act and Rule 10b-5 and seeks compensatory and punitive damages in unspecified amounts.

* Dennis C. Foss v. Bre-X Minerals, Ltd., David G. Walsh, and John Felderhof. 97 Civ. 2298, United States District Court, Southern District of New York. This is a purported class action in which plaintiff alleges violations of Section 10(b) and 20(a) of the Securities Exchange Act and Rule 10b-5, and asserts claims of common law fraud. The complaint seeks compensatory damages in an unspecified amount.

* Reuven Randall Singer v. Bre-X Minerals, Ltd., David G. Walsh, John Felderhof, Jeanette Walsh, T. Stephen McAnulty, John Thorpe, and Rosario Francisco, 97 Civ. 2274, United States District Court, Southern District of New York. This is a purported class Action in which plaintiff alleges violations of Sections 10(b) and 20(a) of the Securities Exchange Act and Rule 10b-5 and asserts claims of common law fraud. The complaint seeks compensatory damages in an unspecified amount.

* Benjamin Kemper v. Bre-X Minerals Ltd., John B. Felderhof, Jeanette Walsh, T. Stephen McAnulty, John Thorpe and David Walsh, 97 Civ 2272, United States District Court, Southern District of New York. This is a purported class action in which plaintiff alleges violations of Sections 10(b) and 20(a) of the Securities Exchange Act and Rule 10b-5, and asserts claims of common law negligent misrepresentation and fraud. The complaint seeks compensatory damages in an unspecified amount.

* Scott Wilding v. Bre-X Minerals, Ltd., Bresea Resources Ltd., David G. Walsh, and John B. Felderhof, C. 97-1101, United States District Court, Northern District of California. This is a purported class action in which plaintiff alleges violations of Section 10(b) and 20(a) of the Securities Exchange Act and Rule 10b-5. The complaint seeks compensatory damages in an unspecified amount.

* John Quick, Russell Schroeder, John and Marian McCarthy, and Patricia Hunt v. Bre-X Minerals Ltd., David G. Walsh, and John B. Felderhof, Jeanette Walsh, P.T. Kilborn Pakar Rekayasa, Kilborn Engineering Pacific Ltd., SNC-Lavalin Group Inc., United States District Court, Western District of Texas, Del Rio Division. This is a purported class action in which plaintiffs allege violations of the Securities Exchange Act and regulations and rules promulgated thereunder or other governing or appropriate laws, and the Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act, and assert claims of common law fraud and misrepresentation. The complaint seeks compensatory and punitive damages in unspecified amounts.

* Melvin B. Miller v. Bre-X Minerals, David Walsh, and John Felderhof, United States District Court, Western District of Washington. This is a purported class action in which plaintiff alleges violations of Section 10(b) and 20(a) of the Securities Exchange Act and Rule 10b-5. The complaint seeks compensatory damages in an unspecified amount.

* Bre-X understands that an action has been commenced in the Ontario Court (General Division) entitled Donald Carom and 3218520 Canada Inc., Plaintiffs against Bre-X Minerals Ltd., David G. Walsh, Jeanette Walsh, T. Stephen McAnulty, John Felderhof, SNC-Lavalin Group Inc., Kilborn Engineering Pacific Ltd., Kilborn SNC-Lavalin Inc. and P.T. Kilborn Pakar Rekayasa, Defendants.

The substance of the factual allegations in the Claim annexed to the Notice of Action, which signals the institution of proceeding under the Class Proceedings Act, 1992, appears to be the same as that noted above for the claims asserted in the United States. Plaintiffs allege conspiracy, negligence and fraudulent representation, and seek compensatory and punitive damages in unspecified amounts.
((Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8100))
